summary: The appeal challenged the Delhi High Court's decision to set aside the premature retirement of Head Constable Om Prakash under Rule 56(j) of the Fundamental Rules and Rule 48(1)(b) of CCS (Pension) Rules, 1972. The High Court had held that penalties prior to promotion in 2000 and uncommunicated ACRs could not be considered. The Supreme Court held that adverse entries, even if uncommunicated or predating promotion, are relevant when assessing retention in service. Reliance was placed on settled precedent that compulsory retirement is not punitive, requires no speaking order, and is subject only to judicial review for mala fides, arbitrariness, or perversity. The High Court was found to have erred in disregarding the entire service record, including post-promotion penalties and uncommunicated ACRs.

final_judgment: The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court's order, and restored the order of premature retirement of the respondent.
